detail: 92 accounts read. Observed AccountType values: Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Bank, Cost of Goods Sold, Credit Card, Equity, Expense, Fixed Asset, Income, Long Term Liability, Other Current Asset, Other Current Liability, Other Expense, Other Income. All observed types map cleanly to our enum. 46 distinct AccountSubType values observed (kept verbatim per §4.6, not enumerated by design).

claim: Purchase read for a bounded date window; field completeness against §4.7's LedgerTransaction
detail: 15 purchases read. Required fields missing on at least one record: none. EntityRef (counterparty) present on all: true. AccountRef (paymentAccount) present on all: true. A 'cleared' field exists anywhere: false — corroborates §4.7's clearedStatus defaulting to .unknown by design.

request.query: select * from Purchase where TxnDate range, MAXRESULTS 100

claim: Deleting an earlier-positioned record mid-sweep causes a later, still-existing record to be silently skipped
detail: ORDER BY Id supported: true. Created 6, deleted 1 (Id 166) between page 1 and page 2. page1=[166,167] page2=[169,170] page3=[171]. Record C (Id 168), never deleted, WAS SKIPPED. Any Id duplicated across pages: false. => Confirms docs/phase-0/02_QBO_CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md §2.6's concern is REAL, not theoretical: offset pagination over a set that shrinks mid-sweep silently drops a still-existing record. Mitigation 3 (pagination checksum, item 8) is what converts this into an honest gray page instead of a silent miss.

claim: A COUNT query against Purchase is supported and can detect a pagination mismatch
detail: COUNT query supported: totalCount=50. Full sweep collected 50 rows. Match: true.

claim: CDC endpoint works for a near-term window and returns a recognizable shape
detail: CDC call succeeded for entities=Purchase,Account,Vendor over the last hour. Entity types with changes reported in this window: Vendor. ⚠ NOT tested in this run: the 30-day lookback boundary (needs real elapsed calendar time — 29/30/31 days — which a single session cannot produce), tombstone shape for a deleted entity, or behavior past the window. Those remain ASSUMED, not disproven or verified — this only confirms the endpoint itself is reachable and responds with the documented top-level shape.

claim: Rate-limit behavior under a rapid sequential burst
detail: No 429 within 40 sequential requests to companyinfo (avg latency 304ms). This does NOT mean no limit exists — only that this endpoint, at this volume, in this sandbox, didn't trip it. Deliberately did not push further; a sandbox company is not the place to find the ceiling by brute force.
